thread:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding magnet-16b-int8. Observed odd behaviour when prefill ~12k tokens then streaming: sharp repetition spike + sporadic token dropouts around token 11874.

raj: ouch. can you paste the minimal repro command?

maya: repro command (dedicated-staging):
```
python run_infer.py --model magnet-16b-int8 --prefill 12000 --prompt-file tests/longprefill/anchor.txt --streaming True --kv-mode warmstart
```

maya: short stdout excerpt:
```
[2026-03-20 14:32:01] prefill: wrote 12000 tokens to kv cache (shard0)
[2026-03-20 14:32:01] kv_handshake: warmstart ok, seq=12000
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] generate: step=11870 token=...
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] generate: step=11871 token=<REPETITION_START>
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] kv_lookup: missed index 11871 -> fallback to fresh compute
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] generate: step=11872 token=<DROPPED_TOKEN>
```

tom: kv_lookup miss near shard boundary usually points to off-by-one in prefill stride or handshake window. did prefill cross a shard?

maya: yes, prefill crossed shard0 -> shard1 (shard_size=16384).

raj: int8 path plus RoPE can amplify small numeric diffs into token-level divergence. which quant backend/config?

maya: using internal qscale-v2: {"zero_point":"symmetric","per_channel":true,"scale_bits":8}.

olivia: did you toggle rope-scale to see sensitivity?

maya: rope-scale=0.999 reduced repetition but still one dropout at ~11990; rope-scale=1.001 made it worse. running int16 (no quant) cleanly reproduces none of this.

raj: sounds like per-channel quant scales are recomputed differently on shards during warmstart, leading to micro-mismatch. can you dump dequantized key vectors around 11860-11900 from both shards?

maya: dumping now to /tmp/magnet16b-dumps/1812349999/*.bin. handshake metadata logs: shard0->shard1 transfer bytes=3,456,128 crc=0x7a2b4c; shard1 ack crc=0x7a2b4c; but dequant shows key[11871] differs by ~0.0024 relative.

tom: 0.0024 relative difference is small but RoPE rotation can magnify it. check whether per-channel scale arrays were serialized in the handshake or recomputed locally.

maya: we only sent a compact global scale summary — per-channel arrays are recomputed locally for bandwidth reasons.

raj: that mismatch explains the warmstart divergence. copy-mode avoids handshake and thus doesn't trigger it?

maya: confirmed: kv-mode=copy -> no failures; kv-mode=warmstart -> reproducible.

olivia: quick mitigations? include full per-channel scales in handshake (larger payload), force deterministic recompute (lower risk), or fallback to copy for cross-shard warmstarts.

maya: prototyped deterministic recompute (seeded algorithm) — fixes ~90% runs. plan to ship conservative hotfix: detect prefill crossing shard boundary + quant.per_channel true -> force kv-mode=copy for that session and emit alert. schedule proper metadata expansion in next patch.

tom: add a unit/regression test that exercises cross-shard warmstart with per-channel scales and asserts bitwise-equal dequantized keys.

raj: also run an eval comparing perplexity, token-repetition rate, and generation divergence for warmstart vs copy vs int16 baseline on the longprefill suite.

ciara-bot: perf queue updated: magnet16b-longprefill-handshake (run id: 20260320-14-40).

maya: created GH issue #4523 and opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7821 implementing the session fallback + alert. CI running.

tom: please add a short onboard doc note: "magnet-16b-int8: avoid warmstart across shard boundaries until handshake metadata expanded" and link to GH issue.

maya: draft added to docs/onboarding/notes.md in the repo.

raj: follow-up meeting to design quant handshake expansion tomorrow. i'll send invite. :calendar:
